leftEvidence.role: Confession, suffering, and the coming Kingdom
leftEvidence.title: Mark joins the Christ confession to a Kingdom saying

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Peter calls Jesus the Christ; Jesus teaches that the Son of Man must suffer, die, and rise.
points.right: After six days Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Peter is rebuked, the crowd hears the cost of following, and some are promised sight of God’s Kingdom come with power.
points.right: Elijah and Moses appear speaking with Jesus; Peter proposes tents because he does not know what to say, a cloud overshadows them, and the voice commands listening.

payload.posture: Mark places the transfiguration directly after the promise that some will see God’s Kingdom come with power.

rightEvidence.title: Mark preserves dazzling clothes and Peter’s fear

payload.tension: Mark preserves the sequence without giving a one-sentence identification of promise and event.
payload.title: Kingdom with power and Mark’s mountain
